title: Client Smart Prefetch and Early Tool Synthesis — PRD sketch
content:
Summary:
This doc proposes a minimal surface and SDK ergonomics for "early tool synthesis" and client-side smart prefetching in Hosted API streaming calls. The goal is to reduce perceived latency for tool-heavy UX (search augmentation, action-bridging assistants) while keeping payload sizes small and maintaining safety/fallthrough semantics.

Problem statement:
- Many apps call downstream tools after the model suggests a structured action. Round-trip time to confirm and resolve tool calls creates visible UX friction.
- Naive prefetching wastes bandwidth and may trigger unwanted side-effects (billing, audit surface).
- Streaming partial output today is opaque about confidence and actionable readiness — clients cannot safely pre-render or prefetch.

Proposed idea (high level):
1) Add small "synthesis frames" in the incremental stream: compact typed hints about likely tool calls and their confidence. Frames are informational (non-authoritative) until final commit arrives.
2) SDKs expose a PrefetchManager that can prewarm resources (cache, small read-only tool queries) using a safe, read-only prefetch mode. PrefetchManager decisions are guided by confidence thresholds and policy.
3) Introduce a "batched-commit" API for tool calls: clients can stage multiple candidate tool calls and commit a selected set atomically when the final action arrives.

Streaming frame sketch (frame-level primitives):
- frame.type: one of ["text", "synthesis_hint", "partial_structure", "commit_notice"]
- synthesis_hint.payload: { action_type, args_preview, confidence_score, estimated_size_bytes }
- partial_structure: small JSON-LD style compact object with schema_id and abbreviated keys
- commit_notice: authoritative instruction (tool call to run, tool_id, args)

Note: the SDK will treat synthesis_hint as advisory. No side-effects should be permitted from synthesis_hint alone. Only commit_notice triggers tool execution unless user opts-in to aggressive prefetch (opt-in only and logged).

SDK ergonomics (JS + mobile):
- streaming.on('frame', fn) -> frames delivered as they arrive, with a helper frame.isActionable boolean
- PrefetchManager.prefetch(hint): returns a token representing a prefetch task, cancelable, and surfaced in telemetry
- ToolsClient.stage(toolId, argsPreview) -> stagingHandle; ToolsClient.commit(handle) -> executes; ToolsClient.discard(handle)
- Defaults: prefetch confidence threshold = 0.85, max parallel prefetches = 3, prefetch mode = "read-only"

Developer UX examples (sketch):
- Mobile app sees synthesis_hint for search.results with confidence 0.92, SDK prefetches a cached read-only API (no billing), prepares thumbnails. When commit_notice arrives, thumbnails are already available and UI shows near-instant results.
- Web assistant receives low-confidence hints (0.55); SDK does not prefetch but shows progressive UI placeholder.

Safety and compliance constraints:
- Prefetch must be limited to idempotent, read-only operations. No writes, transactions, or charged operations allowed unless explicit user consent.
- Prefetch attempts should be clearly logged per-customer for audit.
- Policy: synthesis_hint must never contain PII in raw form; schema must support tokens/ids only.

Telemetry + success metrics:
- Time-to-first-tool-render (ms) before/after prefetch
- Prefetch hit ratio (prefetched resources used on commit)
- % prefetch tasks canceled due to low-confidence
- Bandwidth cost delta (bytes per session)
- Safety incidents: prefetch-triggered unauthorized calls (target 0)

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Server: stream includes synthesis_hint frames when model suggests tool-like outputs; hint schema stable for 1 week.
- SDK: JS and Android implement PrefetchManager with opt-in policy, expose staging API, and example app using staged commits.
- UX: Two product integration demos (search-augmented chat and calendar assistant) show >=30% reduction in perceived tool latency.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal alpha with solutions engineering (2 weeks) — add logs and toggle.
2) Closed beta with 3 customers (4–6 weeks).
3) Public SDK release with feature gates + telemetry (8–12 weeks).

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to self):
- How to design hint schema so it remains compact but expressive? TL;DR: favor schema_id plus compressed arg tokens (no full text).
- Prefetch policies per-customer (SLA tiers might get different thresholds) — tie to Dedicated vs Hosted quotas?
- Interaction with caching layers (edge vs origin) — PrefetchManager should prefer edge-ready fetches.
- Risk: clients may misuse staging API to queue writes; need server-side enforcement of read-only prefetch token.

Implementation TODOs:
- [ ] Draft synthesis_hint protobuf and wire encoding for streaming frames (size micro-bench).
- [ ] JS SDK API PR for PrefetchManager + staging primitives. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/789
- [ ] Add linear ticket to track telemetry spec: RED-4123
- [ ] Security review: partner with security and compliance to validate no PII leakage

Appendix — quick sketch of wire example (pseudo-JSON for readability):
--- stream chunk (advisory) ---
{ "frame_type": "synthesis_hint", "payload": { "action_type": "search_query", "args_preview": { "query_tokens": ["best", "coffee", "nearby"], "radius_km": 5 }, "confidence": 0.92 } }
--- later ---
{ "frame_type": "commit_notice", "payload": { "tool_id": "search-service", "args": { "q": "best coffee near me", "radius_km": 5 } } }

Quick UX checklist for demos:
- demo-1: chat -> search prefetch -> thumbnails ready on commit
- demo-2: calendar assistant suggests 3 time slots; prefetch availability checks in read-only mode

Notes: this is intentionally a lightweight PRD sketch. I want feedback on the minimal wire primitives and whether a staging/batched-commit pattern is valuable, or if teams prefer a simpler "pre-resolve cache" pattern.

Comments welcome — ping in #product-hosted-api or drop thoughts in RED-4123.
